title: BSA Committee Meeting – July 10, 2026
text:
Wesley Tran: Okay, let's get started. It's two o'clock, we have all three committee members. Agenda today: one, the open alert on the high-risk member c_0086; two, BSAWatch tuning after last month's false positive spike; three, the quarterly training refresh; and four, anything for the examiner prep list. Chris, you've got the casework, so start us off.
Chris Burgess: Thanks, Wesley. So the case is ⟨NAME_0086⟩, individual member, joined October of last year, one share savings account, ⟨ACCT_0176⟩. Risk rating is high. The alert came out of BSAWatch about two weeks ago. Pattern is a series of incoming ACH credits, each under $3,000, followed within a day or two by outbound wires-style activity going to a single counterparty, Glenn, Collins and Black, a Delaware business entity.
Monica Feld: And that's cp_015 in our counterparty table. I pulled the history. Since January there have been eleven incoming ACH credits, total about $27,400, and four outbound transfers totaling roughly $26,100. So the balance basically never builds. It's pass-through.
Wesley Tran: What's the stated purpose on the member file? Employment, business, what?
Chris Burgess: Onboarding says salaried employment and personal savings only. No business activity declared. That's the mismatch. The inbound originators are a mix, a couple of payment processors and some individuals. Nothing that looks like payroll.
Monica Feld: I'd also flag that the counterparty details came in through the member's outbound instructions. The beneficiary banking details on file, the ⟨IBAN_0007⟩ and the ⟨SWIFT_0007⟩, were entered manually twice with slightly different formatting. Could be nothing, could be someone being careless, but I noted it.
Wesley Tran: Okay. Did we try contacting the member?
Chris Burgess: Zachary Powers is the member advocate and relationship owner. He called the number on file, ⟨PHONE_0085⟩, twice, and left a voicemail. We also sent a secure message to ⟨EMAIL_0086⟩. No response yet. I don't want to push too hard since we don't want to tip off anything if this ends up being a SAR.
Wesley Tran: Agreed. Let's not have Zachary discuss suspicion, just a routine account review outreach. Are we verifying identity data again? I want to be sure the profile is current.
Monica Feld: I ran the CIP refresh. The address of record, ⟨ADDRESS_0081⟩, matches the last mailing that wasn't returned. The SSN on file, ⟨SSN_0080⟩, passes verification, and the date of birth, ⟨DOB_0080⟩, is consistent with the ID scanned at opening. So identity looks solid. It's the activity that concerns me, not the identity.
Wesley Tran: Good. Is there any chance the account is being used as a money mule account, with a third party controlling it?
Chris Burgess: That's my working theory. Quick ramp-up of inbound, immediate outbound, and the online login history shows access from several different devices in a short window. I'll ask IT through Andre Dubois's team for the MemberSSO login detail so we can look at that more closely.
Wesley Tran: Fine. What's your recommendation on timing?
Chris Burgess: Open a formal investigation now, keep the account open under enhanced monitoring for thirty days, and make the SAR decision at the next committee meeting unless something escalates. If the outbound pace increases, I'd come back to you for a restriction.
Wesley Tran: I'm okay with that. Decision: case stays open, enhanced monitoring, SAR decision on the August meeting, earlier if activity changes. Chris owns the case and the narrative draft. Monica, you handle the counterparty research on cp_015.
Monica Feld: Will do. I'll check the Delaware registry, adverse media, and whether other members have sent to that same entity.
Wesley Tran: Good. Now second item, BSAWatch tuning. Monica?
Monica Feld: So June we had around 140 alerts on the structuring scenario, and 118 were closed as false positives. A big chunk were members making regular deposits just under the threshold for legitimate reasons, like a small business doing weekly cash deposits. I'd like to propose raising the aggregation window on that rule from three days to five and adding a suppression for members with documented cash-intensive business profiles.
Chris Burgess: I'm a little wary of the suppression. That's exactly the profile that can hide structuring. Could we instead lower the priority rather than suppress?
Monica Feld: That works. Lower priority, still generates an alert, but routes to the second queue.
Wesley Tran: I prefer that. Don't suppress anything outright. Also, BSAWatch depends on CoreBanking and ACHHub, so any change needs to be tested when those feeds are stable. Monica, work with Hector Salas on a test environment run, and bring me the before and after alert counts.
Monica Feld: Understood. I'll aim for a result by July 24.
Wesley Tran: Third item, training. Chris?
Chris Burgess: The annual refresh is due by the end of September. I'd like to include a module on mule account typologies, using anonymized elements from this case, and a short one for tellers on recognizing third-party coaching at the window. Paul Jensen's team will need to schedule the floor staff.
Wesley Tran: Good, I'll email Paul about scheduling. Chris, draft the content outline by August 7.
Chris Burgess: Will do.
Wesley Tran: Last item, exam prep. The examiner list asks for our independent testing report and the risk assessment update. Monica, is the risk assessment current?
Monica Feld: Mostly. I still need to add the new ACH origination volumes from ACHHub. I can finish that by July 31.
Wesley Tran: Okay. Let me recap the action items. Chris, case ownership and narrative, SAR recommendation for August, plus the MemberSSO login request to Andre's team this week, and the training outline by August 7. Monica, cp_015 research, BSAWatch tuning test with Hector by July 24, and the risk assessment update by July 31. I'll talk to Paul about training logistics and tell Zachary to keep outreach routine. Anything else?
Chris Burgess: No, that covers it.
Monica Feld: Nothing from me.
Wesley Tran: Great. Thanks, everyone. We're adjourned.

title: Management team weekly - 2026-07-23
text:
Gloria Ibarra: Okay, let's get started. Thanks everyone for making time over lunch. Agenda today: IT maintenance and the ShareRecon situation, BSA/AML exam prep, lending pipeline, member services staffing, and a quick HR item. Andre, you want to lead off?
Andre Dubois: Sure. Two things. First, the CoreBanking vendor has scheduled its quarterly maintenance window for Saturday, August 8, from 11 PM to 3 AM. Because OnlineBanking, CardProcessor, ACHHub and LoanDesk all depend on CoreBanking, they'll all be affected. We'll put OnlineBanking in read-only messaging mode, and card authorizations will go to stand-in processing.
Rita Solano: For CardProcessor, stand-in limits need to be confirmed before then. I'll check with Timothy on the current limits and make sure they're sensible for a weekend overnight. Also, ACHHub, we don't have a Saturday file window that overlaps, but I'll double-check the Fed schedule for Monday morning receipt.
Andre Dubois: Good. Second item is ShareRecon. The nightly reconciliation scripts failed twice this month and Hector had to rerun them by hand. They're legacy, and the person who wrote the original logic is long gone. I'd like to approve a small project to rewrite the share and GL reconciliation into the data pipeline Amy has been building.
Gloria Ibarra: What's the cost and timeline?
Andre Dubois: Mostly internal time. Amy and Shannon at roughly half capacity for about eight weeks. We'd run old and new in parallel for two full month-ends before turning the scripts off. Outside cost is maybe $6,000 for a test environment.
Rita Solano: Operations would need to sign off on the parallel run. Larry does the GL tie-out every month-end, so he should be part of the validation. I don't want a surprise at quarter end.
Gloria Ibarra: Agreed. I'm approving it, with the condition that the old scripts stay in place until Rita signs off. Andre, project plan by next Thursday.
Andre Dubois: Will do. I'll include a rollback plan.
Gloria Ibarra: Wesley, BSA and exam prep.
Wesley Tran: Thanks. The examiner's pre-exam request list arrived this week. The fieldwork is tentatively the week of September 14. The main items are the BSA/AML risk assessment refresh, the BSAWatch scenario tuning documentation, and training records for all staff. Monica has the tuning documentation mostly drafted. The gap is the training records, which are incomplete for a handful of people.
Michelle Perry: That's on me. I'll pull the completion report from the learning system and chase anyone outstanding. I can have everyone current by August 14.
Wesley Tran: Great. One more thing: BSAWatch depends on both CoreBanking and ACHHub, so during the August 8 window we'll have a gap in monitoring data. Chris will backfill the alerts on Monday, but I want that noted in the log so the examiner sees we handled it deliberately.
Andre Dubois: I'll send you the exact outage start and end times once the vendor confirms them.
Wesley Tran: Perfect.
Gloria Ibarra: Kara, lending.
Kara Nwosu: Pipeline is healthy. Auto volume is up about 12 percent over June, and we're holding turn times to under a business day for most applications. The one pain point is CreditPull. We had intermittent timeouts on Tuesday afternoon, and the underwriters had to retry pulls. Rita Jimenez estimates we lost half a day of throughput.
Andre Dubois: That one is on the bureau side, as far as we can tell. Hector opened a ticket with the vendor and they acknowledged an issue on their end. I'll ask for a root cause write-up.
Kara Nwosu: Please do. Also, we're considering a modest rate promotion for auto refinance in September. I'll bring the pricing proposal to ALCO next week, but I wanted to flag it so Paul's team is ready for questions at the branches.
Paul Jensen: Yes, that helps. Speaking of which, member services. Call volume is running higher than usual since the MFA prompt change on OnlineBanking. A lot of members are confused by the new verification step through MemberSSO. We're averaging about 25 percent more calls on login help than last month.
Andre Dubois: That was the change we pushed on July 9. We could add a short help message on the login screen. Shannon can get that into the next release.
Paul Jensen: That would help a lot. I'd also like a one-page quick guide for the floor. Joanna and Nichole offered to draft it.
Gloria Ibarra: Good. Paul, get the draft to Andre for accuracy review before it goes out. Do we need temporary help on the phones?
Paul Jensen: Not yet. If the volume doesn't come down after the login message goes live, I'll ask for a part-time temp through the end of August. I'll report back at the August 6 meeting.
Michelle Perry: On that, I'd rather start a posting early than scramble. I can have a job description ready as a contingency without actually opening it.
Paul Jensen: Yes, please.
Michelle Perry: Okay. Last HR item: open enrollment materials go out in October, and I'm putting together the benefits renewal summary for the leadership team. Premium increases look like single digits, but I'll know more once the carrier finalizes. I'll circulate it before the August 20 meeting. Also a reminder that annual performance review calibration starts next month, so managers should block time.
Gloria Ibarra: Thanks, Michelle. Anything else before we wrap?
Rita Solano: Just one more. Timothy is out next Friday, so Larry will cover ACH cutoff monitoring.
Gloria Ibarra: Noted. Let me recap the action items. Andre: ShareRecon project plan with rollback by July 30, vendor window times to Wesley and Rita, and the bureau root cause request. Shannon via Andre: login help message in the next release. Rita: confirm CardProcessor stand-in limits and get Larry looped into validation. Michelle: training completion by August 14, contingency job description, benefits summary before August 20. Paul: quick guide draft to Andre, and a phone volume update August 6. Kara: pricing proposal to ALCO. Wesley: exam prep tracking and the monitoring gap note. Good meeting, everyone. Thanks.
Wesley Tran: Thanks, all.
Andre Dubois: Thanks.

title: Loan committee – 2026-08-07
text:
Kara Nwosu: Okay, let's get started, it's three o'clock and I know it's a Friday. Four items today: pipeline snapshot, the two individual files we need decisions on, the CreditPull hiccup from earlier this week, and then action items. Rita, can you start with the pipeline?
Rita Jimenez: Sure. We have eleven consumer and auto applications open in LoanDesk. Six are waiting on stipulations, three are in underwriting, and two are approved pending funding. Average time from application to decision is sitting at about two days, which is better than last month.
Kara Nwosu: Good. Any aged files?
Rita Jimenez: Two are over ten days, both waiting on proof of income from the applicants. Kathleen, one of those is yours.
Kathleen Smith: Yes, I've called twice and sent a reminder through secure message. I'll give them until Wednesday and then we withdraw the application and send the adverse action notice.
Kara Nwosu: Fine. Let's move to the first file. Richard, ⟨NAME_0068⟩.
Richard Marks: Thanks. ⟨NAME_0068⟩ joined us in December, so it's a fairly new relationship. Right now it's just the checking account, ⟨ACCT_0147⟩, with direct deposit coming in steadily. The request is a used auto loan, $24,500, 60 months. Credit score is solid, debt to income comes in at 31 percent, and the loan to value is about 92 percent on the vehicle.
Martin Ford: Is 92 percent inside our guideline for a used vehicle?
Richard Marks: Guideline is 100 percent for tier one credit, so we're fine. The only soft spot is the short history with us. There's no prior loan performance here.
Rita Jimenez: I pulled the bureau file this morning. Clean tradelines, no derogatories, utilization is low. I'd call it a straightforward tier one. The only thing I'd want is verification of the direct deposit employer, which Richard already has.
Richard Marks: Yes, the paystubs are in the file and the employer verification came back yesterday.
Kara Nwosu: Any objection to approving at standard tier one pricing?
Kathleen Smith: None from me. I'd suggest we offer the autopay discount since the deposits already land in the checking account.
Kara Nwosu: Agreed. Approved at tier one rate with the autopay discount. Richard, you'll call ⟨NAME_0068⟩ with the decision?
Richard Marks: Yes, I'll reach out by phone on Monday morning and follow up with the written terms. The contact details are in the file, ⟨PHONE_0067⟩, and I'll send the disclosures to ⟨EMAIL_0068⟩.
Kara Nwosu: Good. Next, ⟨NAME_0077⟩. Rita, this is your member.
Rita Jimenez: Right. ⟨NAME_0077⟩ has been with us since late 2022 and has an existing loan, ⟨ACCT_0165⟩, plus checking at ⟨ACCT_0164⟩. They've asked for a rate review and a possible refinance, because they've paid the loan down well and rates have moved. Payment history is perfect, no late payments in almost four years.
Martin Ford: What's the remaining balance versus the original term?
Rita Jimenez: Roughly $11,800 remaining with 28 months left. The refinance would drop the rate by about a point and a half, and we'd keep the term the same, so there's no extension of risk.
Richard Marks: From the credit side, the risk rating stays low. I reran the analysis and projected yield drops a bit, but retention value is higher than the margin we lose.
Kathleen Smith: I'd rather refinance than lose them to an outside lender. We've seen that happen with a couple of members this quarter.
Kara Nwosu: I agree. Any policy exception needed?
Rita Jimenez: No exception. It's inside the existing rate-match guideline. I just need a fresh income check since the last one is over a year old.
Kara Nwosu: Okay, approved subject to updated income verification. Rita, you own that. If the income check changes anything material, bring it back to me before we reprice.
Rita Jimenez: Will do. I'll email ⟨EMAIL_0077⟩ the document request today and call ⟨PHONE_0076⟩ if nothing arrives by Tuesday.
Kara Nwosu: Third item, CreditPull. Martin, you saw the issue on Wednesday.
Martin Ford: Yes, the bureau pull integration timed out for about forty minutes Wednesday afternoon. Applications couldn't be submitted in LoanDesk during that window, even though CoreBanking was fine. We held three applications and re-ran them after it recovered.
Rita Jimenez: The impact was small, but if it happens during a busy dealer day it could hurt. Do we have a manual fallback?
Kara Nwosu: We have a manual pull through the bureau web portal, but it's slow and it isn't documented well. I'd like to write a short procedure so everyone knows how to use it.
Kathleen Smith: I can draft that. I used it once last year.
Kara Nwosu: Great. Kathleen, please have it circulated by next Friday. I'll also ask Andre in IT to confirm with the vendor what caused the timeout.
Martin Ford: Should we hold new applications during an outage or keep taking them?
Kara Nwosu: Keep taking them, and log them in the pipeline sheet with a timestamp so we can prove the application date for adverse action timing.
Rita Jimenez: That makes sense. I'll add a line to the underwriting checklist.
Kara Nwosu: Okay, let me recap the action items. Richard calls ⟨NAME_0068⟩ Monday with the approval and sends disclosures. Rita collects updated income for ⟨NAME_0077⟩ and reports back before repricing. Kathleen withdraws her aged file Wednesday if documents don't arrive, and drafts the manual credit pull procedure by next Friday. Martin, can you track the CreditPull incident and keep the log of held applications?
Martin Ford: Yes, I'll keep the log and update you if the vendor sends a root cause.
Kara Nwosu: And I'll message Andre about the vendor. Anything else before we close?
Richard Marks: Just a reminder that the quarterly credit quality report is due the 21st. I'll circulate a draft ahead of the next committee.
Kara Nwosu: Thanks, Richard. Next meeting is the same time next Friday. Have a good weekend, everyone.

title: IT vendor check-in
text:
Andre Dubois: Okay, let's get started. Thanks for making time over lunch. Agenda is short: the core vendor's maintenance window next month, the OnlineBanking API throttling issue, the data extract change Amy raised, and then action items. Hector, you've been closest to the vendor, so start us off.
Hector Salas: Sure. The vendor confirmed the CoreBanking patch window for Saturday October 17, starting at 9:00 PM ET and running until roughly 3:00 AM Sunday. They're calling it a quarterly release, with a database patch and a change to the nightly batch scheduler. They said member-facing downtime should be about two hours, but they won't commit to that in writing.
Andre Dubois: That's the part I don't love. CoreBanking is vendor hosted, so we can't see inside the window. Since OnlineBanking depends on it, if the core is down our members see errors in the app even if MemberSSO is fine.
Shannon Sheppard: Right, and last quarter the app showed a generic error page for the whole window. I'd like to put up a proper maintenance banner and have OnlineBanking fail gracefully instead. I can have a static status page ready by the 14th.
Andre Dubois: Good. Does that need a change to MemberSSO?
Shannon Sheppard: No. Login still works, it's only the balance and transaction calls that fail. I'll have the app check a health endpoint for CoreBanking and show the banner when it's unavailable. Small change, but it needs a test pass in staging.
Hector Salas: One more thing on the window. The scheduler change affects when the nightly batch kicks off. That could shift when ShareRecon runs, and those legacy scripts assume the core batch finishes before midnight.
Amy Cole: Yes, that worries me. ShareRecon reads from the core after posting completes. If the vendor moves the batch later, the scripts could pull a partial ledger and we'd get false variances in the GL reconciliation.
Andre Dubois: Can you tell what the new batch timing is?
Hector Salas: I've asked. They owe us the revised schedule by next Wednesday. I'll chase it if it doesn't arrive.
Amy Cole: Then I'll add a guard to ShareRecon so it checks the batch completion flag before it runs, instead of relying on the clock. I can do that this week and test against the vendor's sandbox.
Andre Dubois: Great, please do. Let's log that as IT-482 so it's tracked. Moving on to the API throttling. Shannon, where are we?
Shannon Sheppard: The vendor introduced a rate limit on the core API, and we've been hitting it during the Friday afternoon peak. We saw about a 4 percent rise in timeouts in the mobile app last Friday. The vendor says our current limit is a default tier and they'll raise it for a fee.
Andre Dubois: What's the fee?
Shannon Sheppard: They quoted an increase to the next tier, roughly $1,800 a month. Before we agree, I want to try caching balance lookups for 30 seconds. My estimate is that it cuts our call volume by a third.
Hector Salas: Caching balances makes me a little nervous. Members will expect to see a deposit right away.
Shannon Sheppard: Agreed, so we'd only cache the account summary view, not the post-transaction screens. Anything after a transfer would bypass the cache.
Andre Dubois: Okay. Decision: we try the caching approach first, and we hold off on the paid tier. If timeouts stay above 2 percent after two Fridays, we revisit the upgrade. Shannon, you own that, and please share the before and after numbers.
Shannon Sheppard: Will do. I'll deploy to production the week of October 5 behind a feature flag so we can switch it off quickly.
Andre Dubois: Good. Amy, you had the data extract item.
Amy Cole: Yes. The vendor is retiring the old flat file export at the end of the year and moving to a new API-based extract. Our reporting pipeline and a few of the Compliance feeds consume that flat file today. I did a quick inventory and found five downstream jobs that depend on it.
Andre Dubois: Five, that's more than I expected. Are any tied to BSAWatch?
Amy Cole: One is. BSAWatch pulls through ACHHub and CoreBanking, and there's a secondary nightly file that Compliance uses for reconciliation of alerts. I'll talk to Monica Feld on the Compliance side before we change anything.
Hector Salas: The vendor offered a technical session on the new extract. I can get that scheduled in the next two weeks.
Andre Dubois: Please. Amy, can you put together a migration plan, with each job, owner, and a target cutover date, by October 23? I'd like to be done with all five by mid-November, so we have buffer before the retirement.
Amy Cole: Yes, I can do that. I'll need Hector's help on credentials for the new API.
Hector Salas: No problem. I'll request a sandbox key this week.
Andre Dubois: Anything else for the vendor before we wrap? Any contract items, support escalations?
Hector Salas: Just one. Our support case about the intermittent slow responses on the core is still open, and they asked for logs again. I'll send what we have today and ask for an escalation to their tier two team.
Andre Dubois: Good. Let me recap action items. Hector: get the revised batch schedule by next Wednesday, send logs on the slow response case today, schedule the extract session, and request the sandbox key. Shannon: maintenance banner and health check ready in staging by October 14, and the balance caching rollout the week of October 5 with metrics afterward. Amy: ShareRecon batch completion guard under IT-482 this week, and the extract migration plan by October 23. I'll update the change calendar and tell Member Services about the October 17 window so they can prepare the floor.
Shannon Sheppard: Sounds right to me.
Amy Cole: Same here.
Hector Salas: All good. Thanks, everyone.
Andre Dubois: Thanks, all. We'll reconvene at the next check-in in two weeks.

title: Member services huddle - Friday 2026-10-02
text:
Paul Jensen: Okay, let's get started, it's three o'clock and I know everybody wants to get out of here for the weekend. Quick agenda: one, last night's OnlineBanking login complaints, two, the two member follow-ups from this week, three, teller line coverage for month-end Monday, and four, MemberCRM note hygiene. Anything else to add?
Zachary Powers: Can we squeeze in the lobby wait times? Saturday mornings have been rough.
Paul Jensen: Yep, I'll put that at the end. Zachary, you were fielding the login calls, so start us off.
Zachary Powers: Sure. Between about four and six yesterday we had maybe a dozen members calling because the mobile app kept kicking them back to the sign-in screen after they passed MFA. IT confirmed it was on the MemberSSO side, not CoreBanking, so balances and transactions were fine, people just couldn't get in. Andre's team pushed a fix a little before six. Since then I haven't had a single repeat call.
Nichole Kirk: I had two of those. One member was convinced her account was frozen. I walked her through it and told her it was an identity service issue, not her money.
Joanna Buchanan: Same here. One thing I noticed is MemberCRM was also sluggish during that window. Notes weren't saving.
Paul Jensen: That tracks, MemberCRM depends on MemberSSO, so when SSO hiccups our notes tool goes with it. Joanna, did you lose any notes?
Joanna Buchanan: Two, I had to retype them afterward. I got them in by end of day.
Paul Jensen: Good. Decision: if SSO is flaky again, we jot notes in a shared doc and paste into MemberCRM once it's back, rather than skipping them. Zachary, can you post that guidance in #member-services so it's written down?
Zachary Powers: Will do, I'll post it right after this.
Paul Jensen: Next, member follow-ups. Nichole, you had the one on the savings account.
Nichole Kirk: Yes, ⟨NAME_0046⟩. They called Wednesday asking why a dividend posting looked smaller than expected on the share savings account ⟨ACCT_0103⟩. I checked, and it's because the balance dipped under the minimum for a few days mid-cycle. I explained that, but they'd like something in writing. They prefer email, it's on file as ⟨EMAIL_0046⟩.
Paul Jensen: Okay. Is there any chance we waive anything or is the calculation just correct?
Nichole Kirk: Calculation's correct. No waiver needed, but I want to send a plain-language breakdown. Low risk, been with us since 2018, I'd like to keep it friendly.
Paul Jensen: Agreed. Nichole, send the written breakdown by Tuesday and copy me.
Nichole Kirk: Got it, Tuesday.
Paul Jensen: The other one is mine. ⟨NAME_0058⟩ asked about updating contact preferences on ⟨ACCT_0131⟩. They want text alerts turned on for the share savings account, and the number they gave me is the one we already have, ⟨PHONE_0058⟩. Catherine, can you do the alert setup since you're on the desk Monday?
Catherine Powell: Sure. Do I need to verify them again or is the call from yesterday enough?
Paul Jensen: Do a fresh verification when you call back. Don't rely on my notes for that. Once alerts are enabled, add a line in MemberCRM so we have it on record.
Catherine Powell: Okay, I'll call Monday morning and log it.
Paul Jensen: Thanks. Now month-end coverage. Monday is the last business day of the quarter's first month, so expect heavier traffic, especially cashier's checks and loan payments. Maxwell, Joseph, how are your schedules?
Maxwell Castro: I'm in at eight thirty Monday. I can take the first lunch slot and cover the drive-up.
Joseph Miller: I'm there all day too. Last month the drive-up queue backed up around noon. Could we have a floater from the desk for an hour?
Paul Jensen: Reasonable. Catherine, can you float from eleven thirty to twelve thirty?
Catherine Powell: I can after my alert call. That works.
Paul Jensen: Great. Also, remind members that ACH credits may post a bit later on Monday, so if someone asks why a deposit isn't showing, we point them to the evening posting window and don't promise a time.
Joseph Miller: Understood. I'll put a sticky on the teller station.
Paul Jensen: Fourth item, MemberCRM hygiene. I audited a handful of notes this week and a few were just 'called about account' with nothing else. Please include the reason, what you told them, and any follow-up and owner. Keep personal details out of free text, use the member record fields instead.
Zachary Powers: Is there a template?
Paul Jensen: There's an old one. Zachary, could you refresh it and share it Wednesday?
Zachary Powers: Yep, I'll take that, Wednesday.
Paul Jensen: Last, lobby wait times on Saturday. Joanna, you worked it last week.
Joanna Buchanan: We had two tellers and one advocate, and the line was out the door around ten. Most people just needed a quick deposit or a coin machine receipt. I think we could move one advocate to the front to triage.
Paul Jensen: Let's try that this Saturday. Joanna, you triage at the front from nine thirty to eleven, and we'll count how many we can send to the ATM or app instead.
Joanna Buchanan: Fine by me, I'll keep a tally sheet.
Paul Jensen: Perfect. Recap of action items: Zachary posts the notes-fallback guidance today and sends the refreshed template Wednesday. Nichole sends the dividend breakdown by Tuesday. Catherine verifies and enables text alerts Monday and floats at the drive-up. Joseph handles the teller reminder about ACH timing. Joanna triages and tallies Saturday. Anything missing?
Nichole Kirk: Nope, that's all of it.
Paul Jensen: Great, thanks everyone. Have a good weekend.
